drivers.name: AtlasIED Atmosphere
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls AtlasIED Atmosphere AZM4 and AZM8 audio processing and control systems over the third-party JSON-RPC protocol on TCP port 5321. Covers source / zone / mix / group gain and mute, zone source select, group combine, message and routine and scene playback, GPO state, and today's bell schedule. Subscribes for state updates on connect.

help.overview:
AtlasIED Atmosphere is a configurable audio DSP / mixer / paging system widely deployed in restaurants, retail, fitness, and house-of-worship installs. This driver speaks the third-party JSON-RPC protocol on TCP port 5321. It subscribes to entity state on connect, so updates push live as users change settings on the front panel or in the web UI.

Parameter names are assigned during device configuration (via the Atmosphere web UI). The driver addresses entities by zero-based index — Source 0, Zone 0, etc. Use the Atmosphere web UI's Settings → Third Party Control → Message Table to map names to indices.
help.setup:
1. In the Atmosphere web UI, go to Settings → Third Party Control → General and toggle 'Enable' on for the third-party control API.
2. Confirm the Atmosphere has a static IP (or DHCP reservation).
3. In OpenAVC, enter the IP. Port 5321 is fixed.
4. Set the entity counts (zones, sources, mixes, groups) to match the device configuration. Counts default to AZM8 sizing; over-sizing is harmless but bigger than needed clutters the state list.
5. After connecting, confirm the source / zone / mix / group names from the Atmosphere config show up in the device state.

compatible_models.notes: AZM4 / AZM8 are the standalone DSPs; AZMP4 / AZMP8 add internal amplification but share the same third-party control surface.

drivers.name: Atlona OmniStream
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Atlona OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate AV-over-IP encoders and decoders via the Telnet CLI (port 23). Supports source routing, audio mute/volume, video enable, HDCP, analog speaker power, and CEC/RS-232 display triggers. Runtime control surface only — install-time setup is configured in the device's web UI.

help.overview: Atlona OmniStream is an AV-over-IP encoder/decoder system. Encoders take HDMI sources and produce network streams; decoders pick a stream and output HDMI to a display. Routing happens by setting which IP stream each decoder receives (the VideoInput command).
help.setup:
1. Set a static IP on the OmniStream unit via its web UI. 2. In the web UI, disable Telnet login authentication (IPLogin) so
   this driver can connect without credentials.
3. Configure encoder sessions (multicast addresses, video format)
   and decoder IP inputs in the web UI before driver use.
4. Connect this driver to port 23. The HDMI output index ranges
   1..2 on most decoders; the session index ranges 1..6.
5. Volume range is 0..15 (Atlona's native scale). 6. To route a source: send the "Set Video Input" command with the
   output number and the IP input name (e.g. "ip_input3") configured
   on the decoder's web UI.

compatible_models.notes: All OmniStream Pro, R-Type, and Wallplate models on firmware 2.0+. Some audio commands (mute, volume, AudioInput, AnalogPower, DisplayBtn, VolumeBtn, InputBtn) are Pro-only and silently no-op on R-Type units.

drivers.name: Dante DDM / Director
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Dante audio routing via the Audinate Managed API. Requires Dante Domain Manager or Dante Director Professional. Discover devices, route/unroute audio channels, monitor subscriptions.

help.overview:
This driver connects to a Dante Domain Manager (DDM) or Dante Director Professional instance to control audio routing across all Dante devices on the network. It does NOT connect to individual Dante devices — the DDM/Director acts as the central management point.

You can route any transmit (Tx) channel to any receive (Rx) channel, clear routes, and monitor subscription status.
help.setup:
1. You need Dante Domain Manager (on-premise) or Dante Director Professional (cloud) — the Standard tier does not include API access.
2. Generate an API key in the DDM/Director web UI.
3. Enter the DDM/Director URL (e.g., https://ddm.local or the Director cloud URL).
4. Enter the API key.
5. Enter the Dante domain name to manage (shown in DDM/Director).
6. Use the 'refresh' command to discover devices and channels.

drivers.name: Audio-Technica ATDM-0604
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-0604 Digital SmartMixer via TCP. Supports input/output level and mute control, preset recall, and SmartMix configuration.

help.overview: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-0604 Digital SmartMixer. The ATDM-0604 is a 6-input, 4-output automatic mixer designed for conference and installed sound applications.
help.setup: 1. Connect the ATDM-0604 to the network. 2. The default control port is 17300. 3. Configure the device's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 4. Input channels: 1-6 (mic/line), ST (stereo). 5. Output channels: 1-4, ST (stereo).

drivers.name: Audio-Technica ATDM-1012
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-1012 and ATDM-1012DAN Digital SmartMixers via TCP. Supports input/output level and mute control, bus assign, SmartMix configuration, operator faders, and preset recall.

help.overview: Controls Audio-Technica ATDM-1012 / ATDM-1012DAN Digital SmartMixers. The ATDM-1012 is a 10-input, 8-output automatic mixer with 12 mix buses, designed for conference rooms, courtrooms, and council chambers. The DAN variant adds Dante audio networking.
help.setup: 1. Connect the ATDM-1012 to the network. 2. The default control port is 17300. 3. Configure the device's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 4. Input channels: 1-10 (mic/line), ST1, ST2, Sub 1-8. 5. Output channels: 1-8, ST1, ST2. 6. The ATDM-1012DAN uses the same protocol with added Dante settings.

drivers.name: Behringer X32 Digital Mixer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Behringer X32 and X32 Compact digital mixing consoles via OSC. 32 input channels, 16 mix buses, 6 matrices, 8 DCAs, 8 aux inputs, 8 FX returns, main stereo and mono outputs. Also compatible with Midas M32.

help.overview: Controls a Behringer X32 or X32 Compact digital mixer over the network using the OSC (Open Sound Control) protocol. Full console coverage including all 32 input channels, 16 mix buses, 6 matrices, 8 DCAs, 8 aux inputs, 8 FX returns, and main stereo/mono outputs.
help.setup:
1. Connect the X32 to the same network as the OpenAVC server. 2. On the X32, go to Setup > Network and note the IP address. 3. Enter the IP address in the device config. The default port is 10023. 4. The driver will automatically subscribe to feedback and start
   receiving fader/mute updates.

drivers.name: Biamp Tesira TTP
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Biamp Tesira and TesiraFORTE DSPs via the TTP (Tesira Text Protocol) over TCP port 23. Supports level control, mute, and preset recall. Configure Instance Tags to match your Tesira design file.

help.overview: Controls Biamp Tesira and TesiraFORTE DSPs via the TTP protocol. Supports level control, mute, and preset recall. Configure Instance Tags to match your Tesira design file.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Tesira DSP to the network. 2. Default control port is 23 (Telnet). 3. Set the Instance Tags to match your Tesira design file
   (e.g., "PgmLevel" for the program level fader).
4. Instance Tags are user-assigned labels in the Biamp Tesira software.

compatible_models.notes: Driver supports level, mute, and preset recall — typical conferencing use.

drivers.name: BirdDog NDI Encoder/Decoder
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BirdDog NDI encoders and decoders via REST API. Select NDI sources on decoders, monitor input/output status, reboot, and refresh source lists.

help.overview:
Controls BirdDog NDI encoders and decoders — Mini, Flex, 4K HDMI, 4K SDI, Studio NDI, PLAY, Quad, and similar models.

For decoders: select which NDI source to display, cycle through available sources, and monitor the active source.

For encoders: monitor input status and NDI source name.

No external software, SDK, or runtime required.
help.setup:
1. Enter the device's IP address (find it via BirdDog Central or your network's DHCP table).
2. Default port is 8080.
3. No authentication is required.
4. For decoders, use 'select_source' with the full NDI source name (e.g., 'BIRDDOG-P200 (Camera)').
5. Use 'refresh_sources' to update the available source list.

drivers.name: BirdDog PTZ Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls BirdDog PTZ cameras via REST API and VISCA. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, presets, exposure, white balance, tally, and NDI encode settings.

help.overview:
Controls any BirdDog PTZ camera — P100, P200, P240, P400, A200, A300, X1, MAKI, and newer models. Uses the built-in REST API for configuration and VISCA-over-UDP for real-time PTZ movement.

No external software, SDK, or runtime required.
help.setup:
1. Enter the camera's IP address (find it via the camera's on-screen display or BirdDog Central).
2. Default REST port is 8080, VISCA port is 52381.
3. No authentication is required.
4. Use 'recall_preset' and 'save_preset' with preset numbers (1-255 depending on model).

drivers.name: Blackmagic Videohub
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Blackmagic Design Videohub routers over the Videohub Ethernet Protocol (TCP 9990). Supports video output routing, monitoring output routing, input/output label editing, and output locking across the entire Videohub product line.

help.overview: Blackmagic Videohub is a family of SDI matrix routers used in broadcast, post-production, and live event facilities. This driver speaks the Videohub Ethernet Protocol, used by every Videohub server-class device since 2010. It exposes video routing, monitoring routing, lock state, and label editing as macro-callable commands.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Videohub to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the unit's IP address from the front panel (Smart Videohub) or from Blackmagic Videohub Setup.
3. The Videohub Ethernet Protocol on TCP 9990 is always enabled — no auth, no enable step.
4. Enter the IP address in the device config; leave port at 9990.
5. Outputs and inputs are 1-indexed in commands.
6. Routing 'output X to input Y' sends VIDEO OUTPUT ROUTING with the protocol's 0-indexed values.

compatible_models.notes: All current Videohub products share the v2.3 Ethernet Protocol. Pre-declared state variables cover the first 16 video ports + 4 monitoring outputs; routing on wider frames still works, additional ports surface as raw keys.

drivers.name: Crestron DM NVX
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Crestron DM NVX AV-over-IP encoders and decoders via the REST API. Supports device status, video/audio source selection, stream routing, and AV I/O monitoring.

compatible_models.notes: Any Crestron DM NVX endpoint via REST API.

drivers.name: Extron SIS Protocol
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Extron products via the SIS (Simple Instruction Set) protocol. Covers crosspoint matrix switchers (DXP, CrossPoint), presentation switchers (IN Series), scalers (DSC, DVS), distribution amplifiers, and DSP products. Works over TCP (port 23) or RS-232 (9600 8N1).

help.overview: Universal control for Extron products using the SIS protocol. Works with 200+ products including crosspoint matrix switchers, presentation switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and DSPs.
help.setup: 1. Connect the Extron device to the network or via RS-232 (9600 8N1). 2. For TCP control, set the device's IP address and use port 23 (default). 3. Extron recommends a 100ms delay between commands (pre-configured).

compatible_models.notes: Any Extron product implementing the SIS protocol (~200 products).

drivers.name: Generic HTTP/REST Device
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Template driver for HTTP/REST-controlled devices. Supports JSON APIs with configurable authentication (none, basic, bearer, API key, digest) and optional HTTPS with self-signed certificate support.

help.overview: Template driver for controlling any device with an HTTP or REST API. Install this driver and add your own commands, state variables, and polling using the Driver Builder. Many modern AV devices expose REST APIs alongside traditional serial or TCP protocols.
help.setup:
1. Enter the device's IP address and HTTP port. 2. Configure authentication if the device requires it (basic, bearer,
   API key, or digest).
3. Enable HTTPS if the device uses TLS. Disable certificate verification
   for self-signed certs (common on AV equipment).
4. Use the Driver Builder to add commands and state variables for
   your specific device.

drivers.name: PJLink Class 1 Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls any PJLink Class 1 compatible projector.

help.overview: Universal projector control via the PJLink Class 1 standard. Works with 100+ models from Epson, NEC, Panasonic, Sony, Christie, Hitachi, BenQ, Optoma, Canon, and Vivitek.
help.setup:
1. Enable network control on the projector (varies by manufacturer)
2. Assign a static IP address to the projector
3. If authentication is enabled, set the PJLink password
4. Default port is 4352 (PJLink standard)

drivers.name: Wake-on-LAN
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Send Wake-on-LAN magic packets to wake devices on the network. No persistent connection required.

help.overview: Sends Wake-on-LAN magic packets to power on devices remotely. Works with any Ethernet device that supports WoL (most PCs, NUCs, some displays, and media players).
help.setup:
1. Enable Wake-on-LAN in the target device's BIOS/UEFI settings
2. Enable WoL in the OS network adapter settings
3. Enter the target device's MAC address (e.g. AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF)
4. The broadcast address is usually 255.255.255.255 (default)

drivers.name: Kramer Protocol 3000
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Kramer products via Protocol 3000 over TCP (port 5000). Covers matrix switchers (VS series), scalers (VP series), distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems.

help.overview: Controls Kramer matrix switchers, scalers, distribution amplifiers, and Via wireless presentation systems via Protocol 3000. Common in corporate AV, education, and houses of worship.
help.setup:
1. Connect the switcher to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the IP address via the front panel menu or Kramer Network. 3. Enter the IP address and port 5000 (default) in the device config. 4. Machine number defaults to 01. Change it if multiple Kramer units
   share the same port.

drivers.name: LG SICP Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls LG commercial displays via SICP over TCP (port 9761). Supports power, input, volume, mute, and screen mute. Covers webOS Signage, LED, and OLED commercial series.

help.overview: Controls LG commercial displays via the SICP protocol. Supports power, input selection, volume, mute, and screen mute. Covers webOS Signage, LED, and OLED commercial series.
help.setup: 1. Connect the LG display to the network. 2. Default control port is 9761. 3. Set the Display ID (01-99, or 00 for broadcast to all displays).

drivers.name: LG WebOS
drivers.author: Keaton Stacks
drivers.description: Controls LG WebOS TVs (2016+) via the SSAP WebSocket protocol.

help.overview: Controls LG WebOS televisions using the SSAP protocol over a secure WebSocket connection on port 3001.  Supports power, volume, input switching, and app launching.
help.setup: Enable 'LG Connect Apps' or network control in the TV's General settings. A pairing prompt will appear on the TV screen on first connect. If the prompt does not appear, use the 'Force Pair' command.

drivers.name: Lightware LW3
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Lightware switchers and matrix routers via Protocol #3 (LW3) over TCP port 6107. Covers UCX, Taurus UCX, MMX2, MMX, and MX2M products. Provides video and audio crosspoint switching, mute, lock, HDCP, output 5V, embedded- audio mute, EDID switching, analog audio level/mute/balance, and CEC command sending.

help.overview: Lightware LW3 is the unified ASCII control protocol used across Lightware's matrix switchers, extenders, and modular routers. Commands target a tree of nodes (e.g. /V1/MEDIA/VIDEO/XP) using GET, SET, and CALL operations. The driver exposes the most-used runtime control surface: video and audio routing, mute, HDCP, output power, EDID, analog audio level, and CEC.
help.setup:
1. Connect the Lightware device to the network via Ethernet. 2. Confirm the device's IP address using LDC (Lightware Device Controller)
   or the front-panel display.
3. In LDC's Network tab, ensure the LW3 service on port 6107 is enabled
   and that authentication (IPLogin) is OFF — this driver does not
   authenticate.
4. Enter the IP address and port 6107 in the device config. 5. Use input/output port numbers as integers (I3 → input=3, O2 → output=2).
   Setting input=0 disconnects an output.
6. Polled state covers I1..I4 and O1..O4. Larger devices respond to
   routing commands on any valid port number.

compatible_models.notes: Any Lightware product that implements LW3 (most products since 2012). Polled state covers ports I1..I4 and O1..O4 — adequate for UCX, Taurus, and MMX2; commands accept any port number for larger MX2M frames.

drivers.name: Middle Atlantic RackLink PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Middle Atlantic / Legrand RackLink RLNK power distribution units (Select, Premium, Premium+) over the RackLink Control Protocol on TCP port 60000. Outlet and dry-contact control, sequencing, naming, EPO, and live voltage / current / temperature / wattage telemetry. Premium models push unsolicited status changes; Select models fall back to polling.

help.overview: RackLink is the Middle Atlantic (now Legrand AV) family of network-controlled rack PDUs commonly installed in commercial AV racks. The driver speaks the binary RackLink Control Protocol so macros can switch outlets on / off, cycle outlets to power-cycle frozen gear, sequence the rack up / down, and (on Premium / Premium+ units) read live telemetry.
help.setup:
1. Connect the PDU to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the PDU's IP from the RackLink front panel or web UI.
3. Log into the PDU's web UI as Administrator and set the passwords for Administrator, User, and Control Systems accounts. The control protocol is disabled until those passwords are set.
4. On Premium+ models, enable the control protocol under Device Settings → Network Services → Control Protocol, and enter a username for an admin account that has the control protocol enabled.
5. Enter the IP, port 60000, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC. Default Select / Premium credentials are user / password (whatever was set in step 3).

compatible_models.notes: All RackLink series share the Control Protocol on TCP 60000. Select models support outlet control, naming, sequencing, and dry contacts. Premium and Premium+ add per-system telemetry (voltage, current, wattage, temperature, surge state, occupancy), EPO, and pushed status updates.

drivers.name: Novastar H Series Video Wall Splicer
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Novastar H series video wall splicers via UDP JSON commands. Covers layer operations, preset management, input switching, brightness, fade-to-black, freeze, volume, test patterns, screen color, OSD, and device management. Compatible with H2, H5, H9, H15, H20, and similar models using the H Series Control Protocol.

help.overview: Controls Novastar H series LED video wall splicers. These processors manage LED wall layouts, input routing, presets, and screen settings. Common in large-format LED installations including houses of worship, corporate lobbies, broadcast studios, and live event stages.
help.setup:
1. Connect the processor to the network via Ethernet. 2. Set the processor's IP address via the front panel or web interface. 3. Enter the IP address and port 6000 (default) in the device config. 4. Device ID defaults to 0. If using multiple processors, set the
   device_id config field to match each unit's ID.
5. Screen ID defaults to 0. Set screen_id for multi-screen setups.

drivers.name: PTZOptics Camera
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls PTZOptics PTZ cameras over the VISCA-over-IP protocol on TCP port 5678. Pan, tilt, zoom, focus, preset recall / save / reset, tally light, image flip, auto-exposure mode, white balance mode, and backlight. Polled state covers pan / tilt / zoom / focus position, focus mode, AE mode, WB mode, backlight, and flip settings.

help.overview:
PTZOptics cameras are widely used in classrooms, houses of worship, and conference rooms. This driver speaks raw VISCA over TCP 5678 (no Sony VISCA-over-IP header), which is what PTZOptics cameras actually expose — UDP 1259 also works but TCP gives reliable delivery for absolute-position commands.

VISCA is request/response only. The driver polls the camera every few seconds for pan / tilt / zoom / focus position and exposure / WB state. Joystick-style movement uses pt_up / pt_down / etc. with pt_stop to halt; absolute moves use pt_absolute with explicit pan and tilt positions.
help.setup:
1. Find the camera's IP via the OSD menu, the PTZOptics utility, or your router's DHCP table.
2. Confirm VISCA-over-IP is enabled in the camera's web UI (Settings → Network or Settings → VISCA). Most cameras ship with it on by default.
3. Enter the IP in OpenAVC. Port 5678 is fixed.
4. After connecting, pan_position / tilt_position / zoom_position will populate automatically.
5. Save up to 128 presets (numbered 0–127). 'set preset speed' applies to subsequent recalls.

compatible_models.notes: All PTZOptics cameras share the same VISCA-over-IP command set on TCP 5678. Older models may not support every command (the camera ignores unknown ones). 12X-USB needs PTZOptics' IP/serial bridge for network control.

drivers.name: QSC Q-SYS QRC
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls QSC Q-SYS Core processors via the QRC (Q-SYS Remote Control) protocol over TCP port 1702. Supports named control values, positions, strings, and snapshot recall. Configure Named Control names to match your Q-SYS Designer file.

compatible_models.notes: Any Q-SYS Core via QRC. Requires Named Controls in Q-SYS Designer.

drivers.name: Samsung MDC Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Samsung commercial displays via the MDC (Multiple Display Control) binary protocol over TCP.

help.overview: Controls Samsung commercial displays using the MDC binary protocol. Covers Smart Signage, The Wall, LED, and SMART Signage Platform series.
help.setup:
1. Connect the display to the network
2. Enable MDC protocol in the display's network settings
3. Default port is 1515
4. Set the Display ID to match the display's configuration (default 1)

drivers.name: Sharp NEC Projector
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sharp NEC projectors via the NEC binary control protocol over TCP. Compatible with P, PA, PE, PV, PX, ME, and M series projectors.

help.overview: Full-featured Sharp NEC projector control using the proprietary binary protocol on TCP port 7142. Power, input selection, picture/sound/OSD mute, freeze, shutter, volume, brightness, contrast, sharpness, aspect ratio, eco mode, lens control (zoom/focus/shift), lens memory presets, lamp/laser hours, filter hours, and detailed error status.
help.setup:
1. Connect the projector to the network
2. Enable LAN control in the projector's network settings
3. Assign a static IP address to the projector
4. Default control port is 7142
5. This driver can coexist with PJLink (port 4352)
6. Set Standby Mode to 'Network Standby' or 'Sleep' to allow power-on via network
7. Input terminal codes vary by model — unsupported inputs are rejected gracefully

compatible_models.notes: Per NEC protocol manual. Specific models like NP-P506QL fall under P series.

drivers.name: Shure Networked Devices
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Shure networked audio devices over TCP (port 2202). Covers MXA910/920/710 ceiling microphone arrays, ANI interfaces, P300 IntelliMix processor, and SCM820 automixer.

drivers.name: Sonos Speaker
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sonos speakers via the local UPnP API. Play/pause, volume, mute, track info, and transport control.

help.overview: Controls any Sonos speaker on the local network via UPnP. Works with all Sonos models including One, Five, Beam, Arc, Era, Move, Roam, Port, Amp, and legacy Play/Connect models. No cloud account or API key required.
help.setup:
1. Ensure the Sonos speaker is on the same network
2. Enter the speaker's IP address (find it in the Sonos app under Settings > System > About)
3. Default port is 1400 (do not change)
4. UPnP control must be enabled on the speaker (on by default)

compatible_models.notes: UPnP API stable across all Sonos models.

drivers.name: Sony Bravia Display
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls Sony Bravia TVs and professional displays via the JSON-RPC REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Power, input, volume, mute, navigation, media transport, app launch. Covers Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia models.

help.overview: Controls Sony Bravia displays using the built-in REST API and IRCC remote emulation. Works with Android TV, Google TV, and Pro Bravia series from ~2013 onwards (W, X, Z, A, XR models).
help.setup:
1. Connect the TV to the network.
2. On the TV, go to Settings > Network > Home Network Setup > IP Control.
3. Set Authentication to 'Normal and Pre-Shared Key'.
4. Set a Pre-Shared Key (e.g., '1234').
5. Set Simple IP Control to 'On' (enables power-on over network).
6. Enter the TV's IP address and PSK in the driver config.

drivers.name: vMix
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls vMix video production software via the TCP API. Supports transitions, input switching, audio, overlays, recording, streaming, titles, replay, and PTZ.

help.overview: Full control of vMix video production software. Supports input switching, transitions, audio mixing, overlays, recording/streaming, titles, replay, and PTZ cameras.
help.setup:
1. Open vMix and go to Settings > Web Controller
2. Ensure the TCP API is enabled (default port 8099)
3. Enter the vMix PC's IP address and port below
4. Tally subscription is enabled by default for real-time program/preview tracking

compatible_models.notes: Any vMix edition. Requires TCP API enabled in vMix settings.

drivers.name: WattBox IP-Controlled PDU
drivers.author: OpenAVC
drivers.description: Controls SnapAV WattBox IP-controlled power distribution units over the WattBox Integration Protocol (Telnet, port 23). Supports outlet on/off/toggle/reset, per-outlet naming, auto-reboot configuration, system + per-outlet power metering, and UPS status reporting on units with a connected UPS.

help.overview: WattBox is the SnapAV / Snap One family of IP-controlled power distribution units commonly installed in commercial AV racks. This driver speaks the v1.7 Integration Protocol, letting macros switch outlets on / off / reset, rename outlets, configure auto-reboot, and read live power / UPS telemetry. Use this driver instead of OvrC for local OpenAVC control — OvrC is a separate cloud product.
help.setup:
1. Connect the WattBox to your network via Ethernet.
2. Find the WattBox's IP from the front panel (where applicable) or from the WattBox web interface.
3. In the WattBox web interface, ensure the integration protocol is enabled and confirm the admin username and password.
4. Enter the IP, port 23, and credentials in the device config in OpenAVC.
5. Outlets are 1-indexed in commands. Outlet 0 with the reset action resets every outlet.

compatible_models.notes: All current IP / IPV / IPVM WattBoxes share the v1.7 Integration Protocol. Pre-declared state variables cover 12 outlets; 18-outlet models route correctly, with outlets 13–18 surfacing as raw state keys.
